Subject: Kestrel — order form redlines (derivatives + feedback)

Olga — thanks again for the demo last week. We've got final internal approval to move forward conditional on two IP items in the order form: 1) explicit downstream derivative carveout for outputs used in our SaaS features, and 2) narrow feedback license — Kestrel does not want our product prompts/outputs to be used to retrain models outside of safety/quality ops without opt-in.

I've attached our redlines (Kestrel_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf) and a short one-pager summary. Sara and I are available for a quick call Monday to finalize.

High level asks: 
- Output derivative clause: customer retains title to user-generated outputs/derived product features; Redwood may use aggregate telemetry but not re-train general model weights on Kestrel data without explicit consent.
- Feedback license: allow limited safety/bug fixes and service improvement telemetry, but exclude model training for model release or third-party model suppliers.

Can you confirm whether these are deal-breakers or if there's room for pragmatic language? We prefer a short clause to avoid long redline fights.

Thanks,
Sam

Quick note from my side: we can be flexible on output attribution for downstream productization with tailored carveouts, but we need operational clarity on the "no retrain" language — we often rely on a limited feedback license for safety regressions and to prioritize fixes.

Proposal for the call: 
- Laura to propose narrow language that permits telemetry and safety fixes but explicitly excludes model weight retraining across general models without opt-in.
- Redwood to offer a one-time product credit if Kestrel agrees to allow scoped safety feedback for 12 months (to help with transition).
- Identify the exact fields/data pattern Kestrel wants opt-out for (prompts, outputs, metadata).

Availability: Monday 9/14 between 10:00–12:00 PT works for me. If that's OK, Laura and Ben will join.

Folks — read through Sam's redlines. I'm attaching a short suggested paragraph (Summary_IP_asks_redlined_by_Redwood.docx) but flag the following recommended positions: 

1) Output ownership: Accept customer ownership of "customer outputs" (defined narrowly: content generated directly from customer input) and provide a carveout that allows the customer to use outputs in their product. Redwood will retain model IP and tooling.

2) Feedback license: Agree to a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to use telemetry and de-identified feedback for safety, reliability, and service improvement. Explicitly prohibit using customer-identifiable data to re-train base models or to create derivative models for third parties without separate consent.

3) Timeline & scope: Propose a 12-month scoped safety feedback window with an explicit opt-out for any category of data Kestrel flags (prompts, outputs, or PII). If Kestrel opts out, Redwood will remove the flagged data from product improvement pipelines within 30 days (subject to operational constraints).

4) Commercial concession: Ben — we should offer a modest credit (suggest $20k) in lieu of pushing for a broader training carveout. That keeps legal language tight and preserves Redwood's ability to improve service quality.

If Sam is comfortable with that structure, we can produce a clean redline for their order form tonight and circulate for signature.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Sam — appreciate the clear asks. From a commercial perspective, we're prepared to: 

- Accept the proposed narrow definition of "Customer Outputs" and confirm Redwood won't claim title to those outputs.
- Limit the feedback license to safety/quality telemetry and explicit opt-in for training on private model releases.
- Provide a one-time $20,000 account credit on first invoice upon signature if Kestrel agrees to the scoped feedback window Laura proposed.

If that sounds reasonable, Olga — can you circulate a clean redline incorporating Laura's language? Sam, if you want, we can put the clean redline in DocuSign and aim to close this week.
